notes.title: One Month Post-Launch Summary
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone, I'm Hua. It's been one month since our first Steam indie game, [b]Tongue of Dog[/b], launched on [b]June 2nd[/b]. At this milestone, I'd like to share some project data, insights about our team, reflections on our journey, and our plans moving forward. This serves both as a retrospective on the project and an update for all the players and testers who have followed and supported "Tongue of Dog".[/p][p][b]About the Game[/b][/p][p]Tongue of Dog is a challenging platformer built entirely around the unique mechanic of using a [b]tongue[/b]. You control a dog that [b]cannot run or walk normally[/b]; [b]progression relies solely on grappling and pulling yourself forward with your tongue[/b]. This creates a demanding, easy-to-fall experience reminiscent of games like [i]Jump King[/i] and [i]Getting Over It[/i].[/p][p][b]Development Journey[/b][/p][p]The project folder was created in [b]May 2022[/b] – which feels like "three years ago". Active development started somewhat later, spanning [b]over two years[/b] in total. This was a lengthy and learning-intensive process for our small team.[/p][p][b]Launch & Sales Data[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Official Launch Date:[/b] June 2nd.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Units Sold (1 Month Post-Launch): ~370 units.[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Wishlists Prior to Launch:[/b] ~3,000 units.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Revenue[/b][/p][list][*][p]After Steam's revenue split and US tax withholdings, our net earnings are approximately [b]$714 USD.[/b][/p][/*][/list][p][b]Cost & Profitability[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Development Cost (Financial): $0.[/b] We employed a "[b]beggar-style development[/b]" approach, primarily relying on the [b]unpaid time and effort[/b] of myself and team members during our spare hours.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Did we "Lose"?[/b] Judged by [b]opportunity cost[/b] (e.g., potential earnings from working at a game company during that time), [b]absolutely[/b]. Making indie games isn't solely about profit. To be honest, [b]the financial return is disproportionately low compared to the immense effort invested[/b], and the main responsibility for this falls on my own experience and capabilities as the producer.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Team Acknowledgements[/b][/p][p]While "Tongue of Dog" is a small game, a surprisingly large number of people contributed. As I teach at a school, some [b]colleagues and students[/b] participated:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43425215/f6a12a24d15d9df159150f44c0e21a3cd3c1822c.png"][/img][/p][list][*][p][b]Core Development (Code, Design):[/b] Primarily led by me.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Some Level Design:[/b] Initial design and construction by my students, iterated upon and modified by me.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Art:[/b] Began with my own rudimentary attempts, later significantly enhanced with the [b]valuable participation and support of teachers and students[/b] from our art department.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Story:[/b] [b]Special thanks to Xiaozhou and the students[/b] she led for crafting the narrative.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Critical Programming (Leaderboards & Workshop):[/b] [b]Special thanks to Afei![/b] Afei tackled these technically challenging modules that were beyond my capabilities. Afei and I have collaborated for nearly a decade, starting with our first indie game ArtDiff. Through "Tongue of Dog," he remained steadfast in developing these [b]quirky games[/b] with me – efforts that required [b]significant input yet yielded little financial return[/b].[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Are We Satisfied?[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Looking solely at sales figures? Deeply unsatisfied.[/b] The effort-to-revenue ratio is far too low, falling well short of expectations. [b]This responsibility lies with me.[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Profoundly grateful yet feeling guilty towards participants.[/b] As the producer, my decisions led to contributors investing a lot of hard work without commensurate reward.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Hearteningly:[/b] Many long-time [b]players expressed satisfaction with the final product.[/b] This is incredibly encouraging and heartwarming. [b]A huge thank you to all players for your enduring support and patience![/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Invaluable Lessons Learned:[/b] This project was a precious trial by fire. We [b]gained immense experience[/b], and now have a [b]far clearer direction on how to approach and what to make for our next game.[/b][/p][/*][/list][p][b]Key Advice for Your First Steam Game[/b][/p][p]If you're launching your first game on Steam: [b]Give yourself full permission to make mistakes and experiment![/b] Your first game doesn't need to be perfect or your "dream game." It [i]can[/i] have flaws and shortcomings, as long as [b]the price point honestly reflects the quality delivered.[/b] Crucially: [b]Strive to drastically shorten your development and release cycle![/b] Aim to learn the necessary lessons and navigate the inevitable pitfalls [b]as quickly as possible[/b]. Then, rapidly [b]apply those insights to your next project.[/b][/p][p][b]What's Next?[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Future of "Tongue of Dog":[/b] While the game has flaws we regret, it faces some fundamental challenges. We [b]will not be investing further effort into developing new content[/b]. We [b]will continue to maintain the game and address critical bugs[/b].[/p][/*][*][p][b]The New Game![/b] We are fully committed to developing our [b]next title![/b] Check out the [b]attached concept art[/b] for a hint: it will blend [b]building mechanics[/b], [b]farming elements[/b], and function as a [b]desktop idle game[/b]. Looking forward to sharing more progress soon![/p][/*][*][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43425215/578ca6277d0d6c4792abfc2426e6352147148baa.png"][/img][/p][/*][/list][p][b]Closing Words[/b][/p][p]While the market reception of "Tongue of Dog" was [b]less than ideal[/b], the experience of creating it together, the learning, the bonds formed, and the lessons learned have made it [b]an incredibly rewarding journey for our team![/b][/p][p][b]Sincere thanks to every player and tester who supported "Tongue of Dog"![/b][/p][p][b]Deepest gratitude to everyone who participated in this project – without you, it would never have seen the light of day![/b][/p][p]Let's take these lessons, hold onto the passion, and [b]dive into making our next game![/b][/p]

notes.title: Added "Hide Player Names in Leaderboard" Option​
notes.notes: To improve streaming safety, we've added a new ​​"Hide Rank Username"​​ toggle (enabled in Settings). Streamers can now avoid accidentally displaying other players' IDs. Thanks for your feedback!

notes.title: [Important Announcement] Launch Discount Error and Refund Arrangements
notes.notes:
Dear players,

First and foremost, I must sincerely apologize once again to players who purchased the game at full price during its initial launch. Due to an operational error on my part, the planned 20% launch discount was not activated when the game launched on Steam. Although I immediately contacted Steam Support and eventually had the discount manually applied, this resulted in a period where some players purchased the game at full price before the discount became active.

​​This situation is deeply unfair and contradicts our intention to provide equal benefits for early supporters. I am incredibly sorry and regretful!​​

To make up for this oversight, ensure fairness, and fully appreciate the support of our launch players, I have communicated with the Steam Team and reached an agreement: ​​All players who purchased the game at full price during the period before the discount was activated are eligible for an unconditional refund, regardless of your game playtime.​​

​​Important Refund Instructions:​​

​​Eligible Players:​​ Players who purchased the game ​​before​​ the launch discount was activated.
​​Refund Method:​​
Please visit the Steam Support page: https://help.steampowered.com
Find your purchase record for ​​[Tongue of Dog]​​.
Select ​​"I have a question about this purchase"​​ -> ​​"I'd like to request a refund"​​.
Follow the on-screen instructions.

​​Solving the "Over 2 Hours Playtime" Issue:​​
To assist players with over 2 hours of playtime, whose standard refund request might be automatically denied by the system, ​​please clearly explain the situation in the refund request text box, or simply paste the template text provided below:​​
​​(Please COPY & PASTE the following text into the 'Reason for Refund' box):​​
​​"Refund requested for [Tongue of Dog]. Purchased at full price at launch due to a developer error (launch discount wasn't applied yet). Please approve this refund under this special exception. Thank you!"​​
Pasting this explanation will effectively help Steam Support staff quickly identify that your request falls under this special approval and process your refund.

​​If you experience any issues requesting the refund, please contact us via email (launewbeegame@gmail.com) or Discord (https://discord.gg/5Wxh4WmTbY).

Even after a refund, you are always welcome to repurchase the game during the current discount period or in future sales. We sincerely hope you'll consider returning!

​​Final Words:​​
This error was entirely my responsibility. I am deeply grateful for your understanding and patience. I also extend my sincere thanks to the Steam Support team for their prompt assistance.

To the players affected by this, I offer my deepest apologies once again and urge you to use the refund process outlined above to reclaim the discount you rightfully deserve. Thank you to every player for your support and trust. 

Sincerely,
Hua

notes.title: IMPORTANT: Sincere Apology & Compensation Plan for Launch Discount Error
notes.notes:
Dear Players,

We owe you a profound apology. Due to an operational oversight, our game launched without the planned ​​20% launch discount​​, causing some players to purchase it at full price.

The issue was resolved with Steam support. While the discount is now active, we recognize that ​​players who bought the game at full price before the discount were unfairly disadvantaged​​ — completely contrary to our intent to reward early supporters.

​​We commit to the following:​​

​​All players who purchased the game at full price will receive exclusive compensation;
Compensation details are being finalized in coordination with Steam.

We deeply regret the frustration caused by this error.

For inquiries, contact us at: launewbeegame@gmail.com or via the Steam Discussions.

With sincere apologies,
— Hua

notes.title: We changed from 'Doge' to 'Dog'. What do you think?
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! You know, these days the "doge" meme has gotten all mixed up with crypto and politics. And a bunch of you guys have told us you're not too fond of it.
So, we decided to give it a little makeover! We just swapped "doge" for "dog". It's a small change, but we hope it'll make things more fun for you all.
What do you think of our new name? Let us know in the comments!

notes.title: The game is in the final stages
notes.notes:
Development is nearly complete!

Initially, we planned for eight levels, one of which had an upside-down design. However, after creating two versions, we found it too challenging and decided to cancel it. Consequently, the official version will feature seven levels instead of eight, and we'll offer a discount on the price.

The official version will include the following levels: Origin, Move, Spikes, Ice, Flick, Space, and Magma.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43425215/50c70f95af8ac30a57413660687e082f6aaaf954.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43425215/8d7695859d943730d0499d8d6a6630d450f1c8db.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43425215/68f2d04435b79704cfc46841291802194ca50691.gif[/img]



There's still some artwork and optimization to be done. For instance, we need to replace art materials on the last two levels and decorate and optimize the art on the remaining levels.

Additionally, we have some work left on the game's storyline, including the ending illustrations. There will be two endings in the game.

In summary, we are wrapping up the artwork and optimization work, and the official game will be released soon.

Our plan is to launch the game on Early Access (EA) first. The main goal of this step is to gather feedback from players to further optimize the levels. We also plan to create a new, more challenging 'dark' version for each current level. We'd love to hear your thoughts on this.

notes.title: The game is almost done?
notes.notes:
Let's update the recent progress. The official version of the game now consists of eight levels, which are mostly completed. We are currently working on polishing the levels and improving the artwork. Additionally, we updated the demo version, which currently offers two playable levels.

Previously, the art coordination was handled by the producer, Hua, who is not an artist. However, we are pleased to announce that professional artist Zeng has officially joined our team. With Zeng's expertise, we expect a significant improvement in the artistic expression of the game.

As the level development nears completion, our main focus has shifted to not only testing and refining the levels but also managing the studio's media accounts. Our goal is to increase awareness of the game and attract more players.
